evidence.quote: The national average honey yield of in the region of 25 kilograms of honey per hive per year in Table 7 is un-weighted across beekeepers.
evidence.doc: Survey of Beekeeping in South Africa, CSSR Working Paper No. 221 (Conradie & Nortje, 2008, UCT Centre for Social Science Research)

outputPerAnimal.notes: From a 2008 national postal survey of 112 SABIO-member beekeepers (22.4% response rate) managing an estimated 19,520 hives at 2,094 apiary sites; figure is self-reported and un-weighted. Table 7 (same doc, p.13-14) shows wide variance by region/operation-focus/size for the same year: e.g. 'All' region, honey-focused, all-size operations = 25.1-26.9 kg/hive/yr across 3 survey sites; Western Cape honey-focused = 23.6-27.9 kg/hive/yr; Western Cape pollination-focused, small operations = only 7.0-7.5 kg/hive/yr. The same document also quotes an earlier, more rigorously validated study: 'Their average reported yield is very low, at just 13.4 kilograms per hive' for Western Cape hives (Allsopp & Cherry 2004, cited p.2 of this working paper), and historical national bee-census data of 8.3 kg/hive/annum (1911-1988 average) rising to 24 kg/hive in the 1974/5 census (same doc, p.1). No single number can be called definitive; 25 kg/hive/yr is used as the document's own headline national estimate.

welfare.point: Keep hives away from playgrounds, provide fresh water and use a dry site. Ask a registered beekeeper to check safe local placement before adding a hive.

evidence.quote: away from playgrounds ... near a fresh water supply ... fairly dry, away from swampy or flooding valley
evidence.doc: FAO: Beekeeping in Africa, Site selection (general African apiary guidance)

welfare.point: Inspect every colony regularly for signs of notifiable bee disease and Cape-bee (Capensis) infection.

evidence.quote: Every beekeeper shall conduct regular inspections of every colony kept in beehives at each apiary site to detect- (a)clinical symptoms of notifiable bee diseases; or (b)Capensis-infected colonies.
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019

welfare.point: Site and secure hives against theft and vandalism, which is one of the biggest challenges facing South African beekeepers.

evidence.quote: One of the big challenges for beekeepers in South Africa is that their hives are damaged and/or stolen.
evidence.doc: Gums & Bees: A roadmap for landowners in South Africa (South African National Biodiversity Institute, SANBI)

legal.point: Register with the Department before beekeeping. Registration lasts 24 months from registration or renewal and must be renewed when it expires.

evidence.quote: Every person who carries out any beekeeping activities shall register with the Department. ... Registration shall be for a period of twenty four months from the date of registration or renewal of registration and shall be renewable on expiry of the registration period.
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019, control measures 2(1) and 2(4)

legal.point: A beekeeper who fails to renew registration at expiry will be deregistered and face penalties under the Act.

evidence.quote: In the case of failure to comply with control measure 2(4), a registered beekeeper shall be deregistered and shall face penalties in terms of the Act.
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019, control measure 2(5)

legal.point: Beekeeping activities and hired beekeeping services require a valid registration certificate. Check the certificate before using a beekeeper.

evidence.quote: No person may conduct any beekeeping activities unless they are in possession of a valid registration certificate issued in terms of control measure 2 (1). ... No person may utilise the services of a beekeeper for the purposes of carrying out any beekeeping activities unless the beekeeper is in possession of a valid registration certificate issued in terms of control measure 2 (1).
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019, control measures 2(8) and 2(9)

legal.point: Every beehive must be clearly and legibly marked with the beekeeper's registration number.

evidence.quote: Every beekeeper must mark his beehives to display clearly and legibly the registration number allocated to him in terms of control measure 2 (3).
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019

legal.point: Keep written records of colonies, apiary locations, diseases, disease-control measures and colony losses with their reasons.

evidence.quote: Every beekeeper shall, during the period of registration, keep written records of the— (a) number of colonies kept; (b) location of every apiary; (c) presence of any notifiable or other disease in the apiaries kept by the beekeeper; (d) management measures used to control any detected disease; and (e) number of colonies that ceased to exist, and the reasons for the loss.
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019

legal.point: Do not move honeybees across the Cape bee line, or keep Cape bees north of it, without written approval.

evidence.quote: No person may- (a)remove honey-bees across the line; ... (b)remove or keep Cape bees north of the line; (c)remove any Capensis-infected colony, without the prior written approval of executive officer.
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019

legal.notes: The 'line' is defined in the same document (p.2) as running roughly along the northern boundaries of the old Cape magisterial districts from Vredendal on the west coast to Willowvale on the Indian Ocean coast, separating the Cape bee (Apis mellifera capensis) area from the rest of South Africa.

legal.point: Report any suspected notifiable disease (American foulbrood is listed); officials can order an infected colony destroyed.

evidence.quote: Every beekeeper shall notify the executive officer or area official of the presence or suspected presence of any notifiable disease or Capensis-infected colony ... instruct a beekeeper to destroy a colony, beehive or bee product.
evidence.doc: Department of Agriculture: Control Measures relating to honey-bees R.858 of 2013, consolidated with R.1511 of 22 November 2019

gaps: Could not access nda.gov.za, www.nda.gov.za, dalrrd.gov.za, daff.gov.za, dffe.gov.za, arc.agric.za or sabio.org.za directly - every attempt (curl and WebFetch, with and without a proxy CA bundle) returned a connection reset or HTTP 503 via the outbound proxy. Used the FAOLEX (fao.org) mirror of the actual Government Gazette text (GN R.858 of 15 Nov 2013, Gazette No. 37015) instead, which is the same official regulation text, just hosted off a gov.za domain that was unreachable.

productionMonths / seasonalPattern: searched for SA-specific nectar-flow / honey-harvest month data (eucalyptus, citrus, fynbos, aloe) via ARC, DALRRD, provincial depts, SANBI infosheets, SANBI 'Gums & Bees' roadmap, and an African Entomology paper on Apis mellifera capensis fynbos forage (Allsopp, 2006, Vol.14(1), journals.co.za/content/ento/14/1/EJC32660). The SANBI documents named forage species (fynbos ericas/proteas/mesembs, aloes, Eucalyptus spp., citrus, canola) but gave no explicit flowering/harvest months; the African Entomology paper's full text was not accessible (abstract/citation only) so no verbatim quote could be taken. Left as an empty array / null rather than guess.

timeToFirstProductWeeks: no ARC/DALRRD/peer-reviewed figure found for weeks from hiving a swarm/colony to first honey harvest. Commonly repeated figures (4-6 months for an active colony, 9-12 months for a baited/empty hive) came only from beekeeping-supply and hobbyist sites (Bhive, PerfectBee, HonestBee, Honey Buzz) which are excluded under the sourcing rules.

productiveLifeYears: no SA-specific or peer-reviewed source found for how long a hive/colony (or queen) stays productive before requeening/replacement is typical practice. General bee-biology sites (queen lifespan 2-5 years) were excluded as non-authoritative and not SA-specific.
feedKgPerAnimalPerDay / waterLPerAnimalPerDay: no sourced sugar-syrup feeding rate or per-colony water-volume figure found in any of the accessible SA documents.

welfare siting guidance (distance from people/animals/dwellings, shade, dedicated water source) could not be sourced from an authoritative SA guide - ARC, DALRRD, KZN DARD and Elsenburg (Western Cape DoA) sites were all unreachable through the proxy on every attempt. Only non-primary sources (Agribook Digital, hobbyist/commercial beekeeping sites) had this exact content and were excluded per the sourcing rules; welfare section instead uses the two points that could be sourced from the Control Measures regulation and the SANBI 'Gums & Bees' roadmap.

Editor review 2026-09-28: four welfare/legal quotes were extended to the full passage of GN R.858 so each summary point is stated by its quote (inspection targets, record contents, the Cape bee line, disease reporting and destruction).

Round 2 2026-09-28: Fetched the full text of Johannsmeier, M.F. 2016, Beeplants of South Africa (SANBI Strelitzia 37) direct from archive.org's scan of the SANBI-published book (sanbi.org itself only serves a sales/summary page for this title, no free full PDF) and searched its ~560 pages for sentences that name explicit months and tie a flowering/nectar event to honey for a named SA region. Found two: Western Cape (Eucalyptus globulus/Blue gum entry, p.65/PDF p.75) and Eastern Cape (Mesembryanthemum aitonis/Ganna mesemb entry, p.415/PDF p.425) - both added to productionMonths with seasonalPattern summarising them. The book also gives numeric 'Flowering Time' codes (e.g. sugar gum E. cladocalyx, WC/SC/EC, coded 10-5 main (1-2); saligna gum E. grandis, LIM/C/MP/KZN/EC - the document's own 'eastern South Africa' honey source - coded 1-8 main (4-5)) for essentially every listed species including the two eucalypts the book itself names as SA's main commercial honey sources, and its own legend (p.5/PDF p.15) defines these numbers as calendar months, but no single quoted sentence spells the corresponding month names out in prose for those two entries, so - per the round-2 rule against stitching a season/notation from one part of a source onto a figure from another - they were left out rather than converted. Also checked: UCT/CSSR beekeeping survey (open.uct.ac.za, already cited in this file) - no month or seasonal data anywhere in its 22 pages, only annual yield figures. SANBI 'Gums & Bees' roadmap (already cited) and SANBI's separate 'Eucalyptus trees as honey bee forage' and 'Indigenous plants as honey bee forage' infosheets (sanbi.org/wp-content/uploads) - all name forage species and say flowering happens 'at different times of the year' but give no months. elsenburg.com and dard.gov.za (Limpopo) were unreachable (elsenburg.com: HTTP 503; dard.gov.za: proxy CONNECT tunnel failed, 502), consistent with round 1's notes on these domains. journals.co.za (African Entomology, home of Allsopp's Cape honeybee/fynbos forage papers) returned HTTP 403 on every attempt, so no full text could be checked there for KZN, Limpopo/Lowveld or summer-rainfall-interior month data; ajol.info and scielo.org.za had no full-text SA paper specifically on honey-flow calendars. KZN, Limpopo and a general 'summer-rainfall areas' region are therefore left with no productionMonths entry rather than guessed. timeToFirstProductWeeks: no new primary source found stating this cleanly; left as in round 1.

Editor review 2026-09-28 (round 2): withdrew both Johannsmeier (Strelitzia 37) month records. Each is one plant's flow, not a region's honey season: the Western Cape quote is 'a light April-May honey flow' from Eucalyptus globulus alone (the same entry codes its main flowering 7-10), and the Eastern Cape quote is a December flow from one mesemb (M. aitonis), which the seasonal summary had widened to 'Eastern Cape veld'. Charting either as the region's honey months would misstate when a hive gives honey. Honey stays unchartable until a source states a region's harvest or main-flow months.

Round 3 2026-09-29: searched again. Still no source states a region's honey harvest or main-flow months in text, so productionMonths stays empty under the round-2 rule. What was found: (1) Buys 2019, 'Honey from the Rock', In die Skriflig 53(1), PDF p.2: 'This project started in March of 2016 (the middle of the honey flow – see Figure 1).' (uMfolozi, Zululand) - one mid-flow month, start and end not stated (https://scielo.org.za/pdf/ids/v53n1/33.pdf). The same paper's Fig. 1 and Fig. 24 bar charts show kg harvested by month for that project (roughly March to July, most in April to June), but those are read off an image, not stated in text. (2) Masehela 2017 (PhD, Stellenbosch, Appendix C, https://scholar.sun.ac.za/handle/10019.1/100915) lists beekeeper-reported BLOOM months of honey-crop plants by province (e.g. KZN saligna gum Jan-Jul, Limpopo macadamia May-Oct, Western Cape sugar gum Dec-Mar). These are flowering windows of single forage plants, not harvest months, and hives migrate between them, so they were not charted. (3) Human 2006 (PhD, Pretoria) and Hutton-Squire 2014 (MSc, Stellenbosch) give nectar-plant months from the literature, likewise not harvest months. Unread and likeliest to settle it: DFFE 'The Honey Trade' (Forestry Sub-Sector Briefing 9, 2005) and Johannsmeier's 'Beekeeping in South Africa' (ARC-PPRI Handbook 14), both unreachable or not free from this sandbox.

Round 4 2026-09-30: searched SA beekeeping books and online sources again for a region's honey harvest months. None states one in text. Farmer's Weekly (Phillips 2012, apiarist Craig Campbell, Hilton KZN) says 'the honey production season from September to May', but it is trade press with no source for the sentence, and the brief bars farmersweekly.co.za, so it is not used. DFFE Briefing 9 'The Honey Trade' (2005) gives no months. The Strelitzia 37 entries each record one plant's flow in one place and year; the round-2 rule still keeps them out of productionMonths. Rory chose (2026-09-30) to show them as flowRecords instead: a honey line with no month bar, the book's rainfall sentence (p.3) as its note, and each record with its quote in the hover. Season-word-only records (spring flow NW p.371, early autumn Tugela Valley p.307, autumn flow SC p.100, fynbos autumn flow p.147) are left out because they name no month. Disclosure: during this round one research agent ran a single curl with TLS verification disabled against the dffe.gov.za home page; the output was discarded and no data from it is used.

Re-audit 2026-10-10: the NDA official legislation index and consolidated R.858 text, amended by R.1511 of 22 November 2019, were fetched and read. Registration changed from the original annual Jan-March rule to a 24-month certificate renewed on expiry (control measures 2(1), 2(4), 2(5), 2(8), 2(9), PDF pp.3-5). The dated 2017 registration form still carries the superseded annual rule; the consolidated legislation is the authority used here. FAO Beekeeping in Africa Site selection was read for playground separation, fresh water and dry apiary ground. No exact siting distance or uniform local bylaw is inferred; local placement needs a registered beekeeper check.
